plainTitle: Four speed cushions and a lower speed limit on Nightstar Road

sources.label: Staff report from the Director, Enforcement and Street Management, Transportation Services

whatIsProposed.text: City Council approved four speed cushions on Nightstar Road, between Morningside Avenue and Mantis Road/Knotwood Crescent/Flower Crescent. Speed cushions are raised bumps that slow cars down.

citations.quote: City Council authorize the installation of traffic calming (four speed cushions) on Nightstar Road, between Morningside Avenue and Mantis Road/Knotwood Crescent/Flower Crescent

whatIsProposed.text: The speed limit on that part of Nightstar Road goes down from 40 km/h to 30 km/h.

citations.quote: City Council reduce the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h on Nightstar Road

whatIsProposed.text: Some parking and stopping rules change near the speed cushions, so that TTC buses can get through. One short-term 30-minute parking spot in front of Thomas Lester Wells Public School will be removed.

citations.quote: Parking amendments on Nightstar Road are required in conjunction with the installation of proposed speed cushions in order for TTC vehicles to be able to navigate the route.
one short term 30-minute parking spot in front of the Thomas Lester Wells Public School will be eliminated

whatIsProposed.text: Heavy vehicles are banned at all times on this part of Nightstar Road. Staff said this fixes a mismatch between the by-law and the posted sign.

citations.quote: City Council prohibit heavy vehicles at all times on Nightstar Road, between Morningside Avenue and Mantis Road/Knotwood Crescent/Flower Crescent.
there is discrepancy between the by-lawed heavy vehicle prohibition and the posted sign on Nightstar Road

why.text: Area residents are worried that drivers go too fast on Nightstar Road. The local councillor asked staff to look into speed cushions.

citations.quote: The residents are concerned that motorists travel at a high rate of speed on Nightstar Road.

why.text: Staff measured speeds in October 2025. Most drivers (85%) went 43 km/h or slower, and 95% went 49 km/h or slower. About 2,700 vehicles use the road each day.

citations.quote: The operating speed, which is the speed at which 85 percent of traffic is travelling at or below, was observed at 43 km/h
The 95th percentile speed, which is the speed at which 95 percent of traffic is travelling at or below, was observed at 49 km/h
24-hour total vehicle volume is 2,700 vehicles

why.text: Staff said these speeds were too low to meet the City's traffic calming policy, so staff did not recommend speed cushions. Council approved them anyway.

citations.quote: The operating speed was recorded at 43 km/h, which is 5 km/h under the required speed of 48 km/h.
Therefore, staff do not recommend the installation of speed cushions on Nightstar Road.

whoIsAffected.text: People who live on or drive along Nightstar Road, in Ward 25 (Scarborough-Rouge Park). The area has homes, Nightstar Park and Thomas Lester Wells Public School.

citations.quote: The land use in the area consists of single-family residential dwellings, Nightstar Park and Thomas Lester Wells Public School.
Ward: 25 - Scarborough - Rouge Park

whoIsAffected.text: TTC riders: the 116, 133 and 939C bus routes use Nightstar Road.

citations.quote: There is Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) service provided by the 116, 133 and 939C bus routes

whoIsAffected.text: Emergency services: speed cushions slow down all vehicles, including ambulances, fire trucks and police. Paramedic Services warned of possible delays, but said it supports safety measures.
whoIsAffected.caveat: Police and Fire Services had not commented when the report was written.

citations.quote: Installing speed cushions will result in slower operating speeds for all vehicles, including emergency service vehicles.
Toronto Paramedic Services responded and advised of potential delays in emergency responses but expressed support for initiatives that enhance community safety.
Toronto Police Service and Toronto Fire Services have not provided comments at the time of writing this report.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Staff estimate the four speed cushions cost $16,000. The money depends on what is available in the 2026 Transportation Services budget.

citations.quote: the estimated cost of installing four speed cushions is $16,000.00
Funding would be subject to availability and competing priorities within the Transportation Services 2026 Capital Budget.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: If there are more approved speed cushion requests than money, the City ranks them. Nightstar Road scored 22 out of 100 points.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The record does not say when the speed cushions will be installed.

citations.quote: funding for approved installations will be prioritized using a Prioritization Score
scored 22 ranking points out of a possible 100

staff.text: Staff recommended against speed cushions, because the speeds measured did not meet the policy. Staff did recommend banning heavy vehicles at all times.

citations.quote: City Council not authorize the installation of speed cushions on Nightstar Road
City Council prohibit heavy vehicles at all times on Nightstar Road

committee.text: Scarborough Community Council went against the staff advice. It recommended the four speed cushions, the lower speed limit and the parking changes, plus the heavy vehicle ban.

citations.quote: This item was considered by Scarborough Community Council on April 1, 2026 and was adopted with amendments.

council.text: City Council approved the community council's version, without changes.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on April 22 and 23, 2026 without amendments.

whatHappensNext.text: The City's item page links this decision to By-law 386-2026. Installation depends on budget and the City's ranking of approved locations.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not give an installation date.

citations.quote: See also By-law 386-2026
funding for approved installations will be prioritized using a Prioritization Score
